{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = 'data/sales.csv'
data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Inspect the data
print("First few rows:")
print(data.head())

print("\nData types:")
print(data.dtypes)

print("\nUnique values in `channel`:")
print(data['channel'].unique())

print("\nUnique values in `customer_segment`:")
print(data['customer_segment'].unique())

print("\nUnique values in `status`:")
print(data['status'].unique())

print("\nExamples of `revenue`:")
print(data['revenue'].head(10))

# Check for QA orders
print("\nNumber of rows with revenue = 999999.99:")
print(data[data['revenue'] == '999999.99'].shape[0])

# Convert `revenue` to float after stripping commas
# First, ensure all revenue strings are valid
print("\nAny non-numeric revenue values?")
print(data['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').str.contains(r'^[0-9]+\.[0-9]{2}$', regex=True).all())

# Strip commas and convert to float
data['revenue_float'] = data['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Check for refunded orders
print("\nNumber of refunded orders:")
print(data[data['status'] == 'refunded'].shape[0])

# Filter for completed orders from loyal customers
loyal_completed = data[(data['customer_segment'] == 'loyal') & (data['status'] == 'completed')]

# Compute mean revenue
mean_revenue = loyal_completed['revenue_float'].mean()

# Print final result
print(f"\nMean revenue of completed orders from loyal customers: {mean_revenue}")

# Output for submission
mean_revenue"}
